subcompetencies.name: Screening, Evaluation, Differential Diagnosis, and Case Formulation of the Patient with or at Risk of Substance Use,

level_1: Uses validated screening and assessment tools
Uses diagnostic criteria to define differential diagnosis while avoiding premature closure
Independently performs comprehensive patient evaluation, including for patients with complex presentations
level_2: Performs biopsychosocial history and targeted physical examination
Addresses inconsistencies in collected information from screening and assessment
Continuously reassesses the patient, adjusting the formulation as new data becomes available
level_3: Organizes, summarizes, and presents information and develops an initial differential diagnosis
Performs comprehensive patient evaluation, including patients with complex presentations, with indirect supervision
Facilitates or leads screening and patient evaluation activities within an organization
level_4: Actively engages patients in discussions of screening and assessment results
Develops a case formulation, including diagnosis, readiness to change, risk of withdrawal and relapse, psychiatric and medical comorbidities, and recovery/living environment
Participates in the ongoing development or evaluation of disease identification and diagnostic criteria
level_5: Incorporates biopsychosocial history, examination, lab, and collateral data into patient evaluation
Teaches validated screening and assessment tools to other health care professionals

subcompetencies.name: Pharmacologic and Non-Pharmacologic Treatment for Substance Use and Addictive Disorders

level_1: Prescribes commonly used evidence-informed pharmacologic agents, with direct supervision, including management of intoxication and withdrawal states
Manages pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic drug interactions for patients using multiple medications or other substances
Independently integrates the principles of motivational interviewing
level_2: Informs patients about non-pharmacologic interventions, including evidence-informed behavioral and psychosocial treatment, with supervision
Participates in the delivery of evidence- based non-pharmacologic interventions
Designs an educational curriculum for fellows or providers in practice
level_3: Prescribes a broad range of pharmacologic agents, with indirect supervision, paying attention to dosing parameters and side effects including ongoing medical treatment
Integrates the principles of motivational interviewing, with indirect supervision
Presents research or scholarship at a regional or national meeting
level_4: Facilitates appropriate non-pharmacologic treatment, tailoring recommendations to patient goals, under direct supervision
Independently manages patients with complex disease states and complex medication regimens
Engages with health system or community organizations to improve patient care
level_5: Employs basic counseling strategies in treatment
Develops a patient- centered treatment plan with continuous reassessment, integrating pharmacologic and non- pharmacologic interventions

subcompetencies.name: Neuroscience of Substance Use and Addictive Disorders

level_1: Describes the basic neuroanatomy and neurophysiology
Describes the neuropharmacology and mechanisms of action of evidence-informed pharmacologic agents
Demonstrates a detailed knowledge of known pharmacology and neuropharmacology of all classes of substances
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of pharmacology of different classes of substances
Demonstrates knowledge of the developmental trajectory and neuroanatomical changes with prolonged substance use
Demonstrates detailed actions of neuropharmacology and mechanisms of action of known and emerging pharmacologic agents
level_3: Describes the mechanism of action for commonly prescribed pharmacologic agents
Demonstrates knowledge of complex pharmacologic and neuropharmacologic interactions of commonly used substances
Designs and teaches a neuroscience teaching module focusing on substance use or addictive disorders
level_4: Describes basic pathophysiology and genetic vulnerability
Demonstrates knowledge of mechanisms of action, metabolism, adverse effects, and interactions of prescribed pharmacologic agents
Participates in research on the neuroscience of substance use or addictive disorders
level_5: Describes the neuropharmacologic differences between commonly used substances
Applies knowledge of the latest research findings into discussions of neuroscience of substance use and addictive disorders

subcompetencies.name: Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation of Substance Use and Addictive Disorders

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of epidemiology
Demonstrates knowledge of common clinical complications
Teaches others about the contributing and protective biopsychosocial factors
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of biopsychosocial factors
Demonstrates knowledge of the limits and strengths of epidemiologic test
Applies detailed knowledge of comorbidities, their presentations, and their complications
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of common clinical presentations
Applies knowledge of the contributing and protective biopsychosocial factors
Applies knowledge of epidemiology and clinical presentation to inform policy
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of epidemiology in heterogenous populations
Integrates knowledge to formulate a prevention plan
Engages in research on substance use and addictive disorders or their interactions and common complications
level_5: Describes the contributing and protective biopsychosocial factors
Applies knowledge of epidemiology to patient care
Develops a teaching module to address complex clinical complications

subcompetencies.name: Treatment Modalities and Interventions in Heterogenous Patient Populations

level_1: Lists the commonly available pharmacologic treatment modalities for management of intoxication and withdrawal
Describes the evidence base for the use of specific non-pharmacologic treatments and interventions
level_2: Lists non-pharmacologic treatments and interventions
Applies the risks, benefits, and limitations of available pharmacotherapies
level_3: Describes the basic theoretical principles underlying the use of evidence-informed pharmacologic treatments
Applies the current evidence for use of behavioral, psychotherapeutic, and psychosocial treatments and interventions
level_4: Describes the basic theoretical principles underlying the use of evidence-informed non- pharmacologic treatments and interventions
Develops a curriculum and teaches others about the pharmacologic and psychosocial treatments
level_5: Describes the evidence base for the use of specific pharmacologic agents
Participates in research on pharmacologic and psychosocial treatments and interventions

subcompetencies.name: Patient Safety and Quality Improvement in Addiction Medicine

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives
Discloses patient safety events to patients and families
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events
Demonstrates the skills required to develop, implement, and analyze a program-based quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies
Identifies, creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives

subcompetencies.name: System Navigation for Patient-Centered Care in Addiction Medicine

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies local and specific population and community health needs, and social determinants of health
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations, effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Advocates for quality patient care and resources for populations and communities with health care needs
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of populations, community health needs, and social determinants of health
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations, effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of patient populations and communities
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care with interprofessional team members
Modifies systems to improve access to care for populations and communities

subcompetencies.name: The Addiction Medicine Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies components of the complex health care system
Analyzes how personal practice affects the system
Begins transition to practice
level_2: Describes cost of care and basic health payment systems, including government, private, public, and uninsured care and different practice models
Uses shared decision making in patient care, taking into consideration payment models
Advocates for or leads change to enhance systems for high-value, efficient, and effective prevention and treatment
level_3: Describes how the components of the complex health care system impact prevention and treatment
Identifies resources and effectively plans for transition to practice
Participates in advocacy activities for health policy to better align payment systems with high-value care
level_4: Delivers cost-effective care while understanding patient specific payment model
Manages the components of the complex health care systems for efficient and effective prevention and treatment
Leads efforts to expand the addiction medicine workforce or practice environments
level_5: Compares the specific transition issues relevant to various practice pathways
Advocates for patient care understanding the limitations of each patient’s payment model

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values to care for a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises conflicting evidence and applies it to guide the care of an individual patient
level_5: Mentors others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth in Addiction Medicine

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with supervision
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data episodically
Uses performance data to evaluate effectiveness of the learning plan, and when necessary, improves it
level_3: Recognizes opportunities to improve
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to adapt goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Mentors others on reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data consistently
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_2: Describes when and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses, including strategies for addressing common barriers
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Mentors others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying informed consent, surrogate decision making, confidentiality, advance directives, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, etc.
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_4: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_5: Takes responsibility for own professionalism lapses
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Proactively implements strategies to ensure the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
Identifies solutions and implements lasting, systematic change that impacts professionalism
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
Independently recognizes limits in knowledge/skills of self or team members
Independently translates self-help behavior into improved patient care
level_2: Is aware of the existence of assistance to help with personal well-being
With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to remediate or improve limits in knowledge/skills of self or team members
level_3: Recognizes limits in knowledge/skills of self or team members, with assistance
Translates self-help behavior into improved patient care, with guidance
Teaches others to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_4: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
With assistance, proposes a plan to remediate or improve limits in knowledge/skills of self or team members
Advises others seeking help for their personal well- being, or when they do not meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviors, if needed

level_1: Uses patient-centered language, appropriate terminology, and non- verbal behavior to demonstrate respect, establish rapport, and reduce stigma

Organizes conversations with patients/families by introducing stakeholders; setting the agenda; eliciting values, goals, and preferences; clarifying expectations; and verifying an understanding of the clinical situation
Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication while accurately communicating one’s own role within the health care system
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters using active listening and patient-centered language
Independently uses shared decision making to align patient/family values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Identifies the need to adjust communication strategies based on assessment of patient/family expectations while understanding their health status and treatment options
When prompted, reflects on consciousness and biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Role models self- awareness practice and educates others to use a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and patient-centered language
With guidance, appropriately delivers medical information and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Completes scholarly activity related to shared decision making in patient/family communication
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication
Models the use of patient- centered language and terminology with patient and family

level_1: Respectfully requests a consultation
Communicates effectively with all health care team members and applies teamwork principles to the care of patients
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
Completes scholarly activity related to interprofessional and team communications
level_2: Respectfully receives a consultation request
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
level_3: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Checks own understanding of consultant recommendations
Role models communication strategies that value input from all health care team members
level_4: Clearly and concisely requests a consultation
Checks understanding of recommendations when providing consultation
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations
level_5: Clearly and concisely responds to a consultation request in a timely manner
Adapts communication style to fit team needs
Develops interdisciplinary health care teams to develop patient-centered care plans

level_1: Records information in the patient record with accuracy and timeliness
Appropriately selects direct (e.g., telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages) forms of communication based on context
level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information, including confidentiality laws surrounding certain diagnoses and substance use disorders
Teaches others how to provide accurate, concise, and timely communication in the patient record
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through one’s notes in the patient record
Teaches appropriate communication techniques regarding patients with substance use disorders
level_4: Demonstrates accurate, timely, and appropriate use of documentation shortcuts

level_5: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
